resources.string: Install Grayjay on your Android TV or Google TV, directly from this phone.
Bring your videos to your TV. We’ll walk you through setup — all you need is this phone and your TV remote.
For Android TV and Google TV
Remove %1$s from this list? Grayjay will stay installed. To revoke this phone’s access, also remove it from the TV’s Wireless debugging settings.
Connect a TV you already use, or install Grayjay from this phone.
Keep your phone and TV on the same home network.
Open Grayjay on your TV and select Sync. Enable it if asked, then scan the pairing QR code with this phone. Approve the connection on your TV.
Sync connects your devices without debugging. To install an update from this phone, use the ADB setup instead.
Enter your TV’s IP address from Settings → Network, or About → Status. We’ll try the standard network debugging port first.
Keep the TV on. If a debugging permission prompt appears, allow this phone. If the connection fails, you can enter a different port.
Grayjay is already installed. You can install this phone’s version, or continue to Sync without reinstalling. Existing TV data will be kept.
Grayjay is ready on %1$s. Link this phone to share subscriptions, playlists, watch later and history.
We’ll open Sync on your TV. Enable it if asked and approve the link request with your remote. Pairing uses Grayjay’s existing encrypted Sync connection.
Share subscriptions, playlists, watch later and history between this device and your TV.
On your TV, enable Sync if asked. Keep its Sync screen open…
Approve the link request on your TV…
Paired. Connecting over your home network…
Sync pairing didn’t finish. Keep the TV’s Sync screen open, approve the request there, and try again.
Enable Sync on your TV and make sure local connections are allowed. If you have an older TV app, install this phone’s version first or pair using its QR code.
You can now turn off ADB on your TV. Grayjay and Sync work without it.
We can open the TV’s developer settings for you. Turn debugging back on only when you want to install another update from this phone.
Using your remote, turn off Wireless debugging and Network debugging or ADB debugging. If USB debugging is on, turn that off too. Then tap Done on this phone.
Menu names vary by TV. If settings didn’t open, go to Settings → System or Device Preferences → Developer options. Done closes this phone’s ADB connection; it does not change the TV’s switches.
Couldn’t open settings remotely. Follow the steps above using your TV remote, then tap Done.
A few quick steps on your TV will let this phone send Grayjay over your home network.

1. Connect your phone and TV to the same Wi-Fi or home network.

2. Keep your TV on and have its remote ready.

3. Open Settings on your TV.
This works with Android TV and Google TV running Android 9 or later. Your TV must offer wireless or network debugging.
On your TV, open Settings with your remote. Scroll down and select System.
On some Android TVs, choose Device Preferences instead. These images show Google TV; your menus may look different.
If your TV uses Device Preferences, you’ll find About there instead.
Scroll down to Android TV OS build or Build. Keep that row selected and press your remote’s OK or centre button 7 times.
Stop when you see “You are now a developer”. Enter your TV’s PIN if asked. If it says you’re already a developer, continue.
Go back to System, or open it from Settings. Scroll down and select Developer options.
On older TVs, go back to Device Preferences instead. Next, we’ll enable wireless or network debugging.
Go back to System or Device Preferences, then open Developer options. Choose the option your TV shows below.
Enable it and allow access on your home network. You’ll see “Pair device with pairing code”.
Some TVs call this ADB debugging. Enable network access; the TV will ask you to allow this phone when it connects.
Can’t find either option? USB debugging alone may not enable network access. This phone-only setup requires your TV to offer network ADB.
On your TV, open Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. Keep that screen open and enter the details shown there.
The pairing code expires when you close that screen. The connection port comes in the next step.
Return to the main Wireless debugging screen on your TV. Enter its IP address and port — this port is different from the pairing port.
Enter your TV’s IP address from Settings → Network or About → Status. Use the port shown in Network debugging, or 5555 if no port is shown.
If your TV asks “Allow USB debugging?”, check that the prompt appeared when you tapped Connect, then allow it. You may need to tap Connect again.
Install this phone’s copy of Grayjay on %1$s.
Keep both devices connected until installation finishes. Existing Grayjay data on your TV will be kept. Sources and subscriptions can be transferred afterwards using Sync.
Installing Grayjay…\nThis may take a few minutes.
Grayjay is installed on %1$s. Open it now and use your remote to explore.
You can turn off debugging on your TV when you’re finished. Turn it back on whenever you want to install an update from this phone.
The connection will close. If installation has already finished on the TV, Grayjay will remain installed.
Enter a valid TV IP address and a port between 1 and 65535. Put the address and port in their separate fields.
Enter the 6-digit pairing code shown on your TV.
Pairing didn’t finish. Open a new pairing code on your TV, check the pairing port, and try again. Both devices must be on the same network.
Couldn’t connect. Check that debugging is on and both devices are on the same network. The connection port can change when debugging is restarted; check it on your TV.
Allow this phone on the TV’s debugging prompt, then connect again. For Wireless debugging, pair again if the TV no longer remembers this phone.
This device doesn’t identify itself as an Android TV or Google TV. Check that you entered your TV’s address.
This version of Grayjay needs Android 9 or later on your TV.
This phone’s Grayjay APK doesn’t include support for your TV’s processor. Install the universal Grayjay APK on this phone, then try again.
Your TV has a differently signed copy of Grayjay. Use a matching release on this phone. Nothing was removed from the TV.
Your TV already has a newer version. Update Grayjay on this phone before trying again.
Your TV needs more free storage. Free some space in its Settings, then try again.
Installation didn’t finish. Check the TV’s connection and available storage, then try again.
Couldn’t open Grayjay remotely. You can open it from your TV’s app list.
Couldn’t read or save your TVs. Close this screen and try again.
TV installation is not included in this Grayjay build.
Couldn’t start the TV connection service. Close this screen and try again.
